lina_support: FYI — ACME flagged a big embeddings regression after they upgraded their plan. tokens/sec looks OK but vectors/sec collapsed (~10k tokens/s -> 450 vectors/s). They report 512-length vectors instead of 768, and retries/429s. Escalating to SRE/ML. cc @kai_sre @omar_ml

kai_sre: Got it, pinging logs. Do we have a request_id or sample payload from them?

lina_support: Request id r-8a3c5f. Sample payload they used: `curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" -d '{"input":["doc1","doc2"],"model":"rwd-embed-large"}' https://api.redwood/v1/embeddings` They said the change happened right after their client update + plan bump.

omar_ml: Quick thought: could be a fallback to a quantized/compat variant with different output dim or a batching K/V cache miss causing slow path. Can we pull server-side model variant for r-8a3c5f?

deploy-bot: Alert: node gpu-uk-12 queue_depth=92% at 2026-03-15T14:12:03Z (sustained 6m) :warning:

kai_sre: Pulled runtime traces — we see heavy queueing on gpu-uk-12 starting 2026-03-15T14:10Z. Noticeable jump in client-side effective batch size (8 -> 64). tokens/sec stayed high because prompts were longer, but vectors/sec collapsed when per-request postprocessing started blocking.

jess_runtime: We also rolled a routing tweak ~14:09 that directed a fraction of traffic to q4-quant variants for cost testing. Those produce 512-d embeddings for this model family. Looks like the routing policy didn't enforce dimension compatibility, so some clients received the lower-dim outputs and client-side validation retried/fallbacked.

lina_support: ACME confirms they started receiving 512-d vectors and their client rejects them -> they retried with smaller concurrency which triggered backpressure/429s on our side. They also saw a billing token spike.

julia_billing: Billing note: token charges increased during window, vector units didn't increase proportionally — likely retries counted as extra token usage. I'll put a temporary billing hold for ACME while we sort root cause. Need confirmed time window and impacted request_ids.

omar_ml: Suggested repro: hit embeddings with concurrency=200, batch_size=auto, model=rwd-embed-large and watch metrics: `vectors/sec`, `tokens/sec`, `kvcache_hit_rate`, and `model_variant` tag. Quick fix: pin `model_version=v1.2.4` (pre-quant routing) to verify. Example config: `{"model_version":"v1.2.4","batch_size":"auto","concurrency":200}`

kai_sre: Rolled a targeted rollback for ACME (pinned them to v1.2.4). Early telemetry: vectors/sec back to ~1.2k/s, gpu-uk-12 queue_depth down to ~20% within 3m.

pat_cs: Let ACME know we've applied a temporary rollback and we'll follow up with a postmortem and timeline. They're expecting a full RCA and permanent fix.

jess_runtime: Root cause summary: routing policy allowed quantized variant without a dimension compatibility guard. That led to mixed-dimension responses for a subset of requests; clients retried and increased effective batching, triggering GPU queueing and throughput collapse. We'll push a patch to add a strict dimension-compatibility check + unit tests, and add an alert on `vectors/sec / tokens/sec` divergence.

lina_support: Filing follow-up ENG ticket ENG-3345 with logs, traces, and customer repro. Assigning to @jess_runtime and @omar_ml. Thanks all :thumbsup:

pat_cs: I'll schedule the customer debrief for tomorrow and include the billing hold until patch is verified.

julia_billing: Will prepare the provisional credit and note the incident for the monthly billing export.

kai_sre: Next ops follow-ups: add a runbook step for 'vector-dim mismatch' with quick rollback and pin guidance, and a dashboard widget for `vectors/sec` vs `tokens/sec` ratio.

lina_support: Closing the slack escalation thread — moving details to ENG-3345 and CS ticket CS-8742.
